name: COPA
description: Choice Of Plausible Alternatives (COPA) is a commonsense causal reasoning benchmark. Each question consists of a premise and two alternatives; the model selects the alternative that more plausibly is either the cause or the effect of the premise. Tests everyday causal knowledge.
reputation: Classic commonsense causal reasoning benchmark; component of SuperGLUE; human performance ~99%; now saturated by modern LLMs
notes: Originally introduced at AAAI Spring Symposium 2011. Incorporated into SuperGLUE in 2019. Contains 500 development and 500 test questions. Questions are evenly split between cause-finding (what caused this?) and effect-finding (what happened as a result?). Now largely saturated. Led to SuperCOPA and XCOPA (cross-lingual versions).
